items.title: Rudy Mazzari Interview, 1959-11-06
items.q: In fact, one time in Indianapolis, he was sitting in the second fiddle doing that and he came in wrong all by himself

ctx.x: What would they like? How did they impress you?

Oh, uh, now, I, one person I liked as a soloist, a famous musician, was Nathan Milstein. I liked him. He was a real nice boy. He, uh, would always talk to everybody. And, in fact, you know, would always show up rehearsals before he was time to come on stage. And he's always, invariably, sit in the second fiddle sessions and read the second fiddle part. In fact, one time in Indianapolis, he was sitting in the second fiddle doing that and he came in wrong all by himself and said, let's go, stop the orchestra. He…
Well, you asked me to ask you about Walter Herbert, who is he?
